take_homes: Output is generic until the agent has my real sources, and a rules file that a fresh agent reads is what keeps that context between sessions.
The agent grades its own work too kindly. I use a cold second reader and trust my own read over its report.
Make the agent write a plan I approve before it touches several files.

monday.move: Write a first rules file for the pricing brief from the pilot-cohort run: which sources to trust, which to flag (the churn article), and how to word things for the CFO. Then run a cold critic on the brief before it goes to the working group.
monday.who: Me. I'll hold off on my team of fourteen until the file is worth sharing.
monday.when: Monday morning, about an hour, ahead of the pricing working group send.
monday.stop_condition: The cold critic flags the same weak claims twice in a row, or the file turns generic.
monday.blocker: My team has no shared place for the context files, so everyone would keep their own copy. The module doesn't address this.

misconception.why: The rules file that a fresh agent reads is what survives, not the prompt wording. It is still a personal-brand exercise, so I only half believe it applies to pricing work, and I'd call it shaken, not changed.

one_line: The rules file and the cold critic are worth the hour. The personal website is not my problem, and about a third of the slides are the same filler paragraph repeated.
